issue 4629 -- what each candidate predicate concludes from the
captures already committed in this directory. No compiler was run;
generated by demo-predicate-trap.py.

  A = match.json           (kind: internal_failure)   <- used
  B = contains "llvm::cast<X>"  (the reported message) <- rejected

capture                               exit        A         B         recorded verdict
------------------------------------  ----------  --------  --------  ----------------
out-main-debug.txt                    0x80000003  match     no-match  repro
variant-interface-min-main-debug.txt  0x00000000  no-match  no-match  no-repro
variant-nointerface-main-debug.txt    0x00000000  no-match  no-match  no-repro
variant-parseerror-main-debug.txt     0x80004005  no-match  no-match  no-repro
variant-syntaxerror-main-debug.txt    0x80004005  no-match  no-match  invalid-probe

Read the out-main-debug.txt row. Predicate B scores the ground-truth
build -- which stops at a DXASSERT and exits 0x80000003 -- as no-match,
because the Debug assert text contains no 'cast<X>' substring at all.
Used as the issue predicate, B reports this crash as FIXED on main and
on every release build whose wording differs, including CE's Linux
build, which prints plain 'cast<X>()' without the 'llvm::' qualifier.

Read the two error controls next. control-parseerror (a missing
semicolon) and control-syntaxerror (an undeclared type) both exit
0x80004005 -- byte-identical to the status the DXC_E_LLVM_CAST_ERROR
path returns -- and neither scores as a reproduction. That is why the
exit code alone cannot be used as the crash test either.
